data.title: Edgy bond investors unconsoled by Bessent's big buyback
data.description:
Key points:
  • US 10-year, 20-year, 30-year bond yields rise after buyback plan
  • Markets expected a more aggressive response, analysts say
  • Focus on larger buyback sizes in future

By Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss

Investors were neither shocked nor awed by the U.S. Treasury's decision to triple the size of its long-dated bond repurchase, keeping bond yields elevated and signaling that persistent unease over the government's mounting debt remains firmly in place.

Treasury said on Wednesday it would buy as much as $6 billion of debt maturing in 10 to 20 years in its next buyback operation, up from a $2 billion maximum previously. The amount was higher than the $4 billion minimum Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent outlined last month as part of an effort to improve liquidity in long-dated debt.

That buyback was undertaken on Thursday, with Treasury buying back $5.187 billion in 10-year notes and 20-year bonds.

But that was not enough to satisfy a market that has become increasingly concerned about the government's capacity to support longer-dated Treasuries at a time when a generally stable economy and expanding deficits are pushing yields up.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose to its highest since November 2023 after the announcement, while the 20-year yield (US20YT=RR) climbed to a three-week peak, as did the 30-year yield (US30YT=RR). Yields rise when prices fall.

U.S. yields extended their rise on Thursday after producer prices increased in August, and oil prices rose above $100 per barrel .

"There was the feeling in the marketplace that the Treasury could have made a statement," said Padhraic Garvey, head of global rates and debt strategy at ING in New York, referencing expectations from some market participants that the buyback could have been as large as $10 billion.

"I suspect this is just the opening gambit."

The market response also underscored the limits of buybacks as a tool for controlling borrowing costs, analysts said. Treasury purchases can improve liquidity in older securities and, at the margin, support long-end prices.

But a $6 billion operation is tiny relative to the roughly $32 trillion Treasury market, analysts said, and does little to alter the broader supply and demand dynamics that have driven yields sharply higher over the last three months. Investors may have also wanted clearer evidence that the $6 billion was a floor rather than a ceiling for future operations.

Speaking a day after the buyback announcement, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told conservative strategist Steve Bannon on Thursday that his job is to keep markets orderly as the economy copes with the Middle East conflict.

"I frequently say, and no one seems to listen, I can't change the equilibrium price," Bessent said, "I am just trying to slow things down, make people step back and look."

MORE SEVERE STRAINS?

Jim Barnes, director of fixed income at Bryn Mawr Trust in Berwyn, Pennsylvania, said investors may have been unnerved by the Treasury's "pro-activeness" in attempting to lower long-dated bond yields, a sign that strains in the Treasury market may be more severe than investors had assumed.

U.S. debt recently surpassed $40 trillion and monthly fiscal deficits have recently dwarfed federal revenue.

"The market is probably thinking that with the Treasury looking at this and trying to keep a ceiling on yields, that it's a bigger problem than what we think it is in terms of the deficits and outstanding debt," he said.

"The $6 billion is not a big amount — it's more the fact they're actively doing it."

The disappointment also reflects changing expectations around Treasury buybacks. Initially viewed as a tool to improve market liquidity, buybacks are increasingly seen by investors as a potential measure to ease supply pressures in longer-dated maturities.

But the larger buyback announcement failed to convince many investors that it would materially improve the supply-demand balance in longer-dated bonds.

For now, the market's response suggests that Treasury faces a high bar to contain yields. A buyback three times larger than its previous operation was not enough to reverse the recent bond selloff, leaving investors to focus on whether Treasury is willing to scale up purchases further as long-term yields rise, or undertake more market-supportive action.

At the end of the day, market participants believe buybacks are a temporary solution to long-term problems.

"Treasury buybacks are unlikely to materially alter the diverse forces raising yields, including widening federal deficits, sticky inflation and increased global bond issuance," said Tony Miano, investment strategy analyst at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.

data.title: JPMorgan: Eight of Nine Developed-Market Central Banks to Lift Rates Soon — WSJ
data.description:
By Angus Berwick

JPMorgan Chase analysts expect eight of the world's nine developed-market central banks to lift interest rates before the end of the year in efforts to tame sticky inflation and commodity price pressures.

In a research note published Thursday, the analysts said they expect rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, Bank of Japan and European Central Bank, as well as from central banks in Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, Norway and Sweden.

They forecast the Bank of Canada to be "the lonesome dove."

JPMorgan said its base case was for the Fed to hold rates next week and lift them in December. The ECB raised rates Thursday, and JPMorgan expects a further hike before year end.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Nvidia Rival Enflame  Soars 206% in Shanghai Debut
data.description:
Nvidia Corp. (NVDA, Financials), the AI-chip leader whose products dominate high-end computing, now faces another well-funded challenger in China.

Enflame Technology surged 206% in its Shanghai trading debut Friday as investors rushed into another domestic alternative to Nvidia.

Retail demand exceeded the available shares by more than 6,000 times. That kind of opening creates a much bigger test.

Enflame reported 2025 revenue of 990 million yuan, or about $147 million, up from 722 million yuan a year earlier. The company has yet to turn a profit.

It intends to use the proceeds to develop fifth- and sixth-generation chips to compete with high-end international products. It's the right time.

Chinese chip suppliers have seen demand soar, helped by U.S. export restrictions and Beijing's drive for semiconductor self-sufficiency. Semiconductor capex in China will rise to $82 billion by 2030, Goldman Sachs estimates.

Other domestic chipmakers also saw huge gains on the first day, highlighting how aggressively investors are betting on China's AI hardware industry.

The 206% boom is just the beginning for investors. Next question: can Enflame translate policy support and strong demand into revenue growth fast enough to justify the valuation investors put on the company on day one.

data.title: Dell, HPE and HP surge on AI enterprise demand and PC, server refresh
data.description:
Dell , Hewlett Packard Enterprise and HP were all surging 8% or more during Friday morning market action due in part to a combination of sustained enterprise AI demand and a PC refresh.

HPE was also boosted due to strong earnings results from Oracle . Earlier this month, the two companies announced a new partnership. Under the terms of the deal, Oracle plans to scale its AI global infrastructure by deploying HPE's routing and switching platforms across all its data centers. This is good news for HPE as Oracle's remaining performance obligations grew $209B during the first quarter to $664B, including more than $30B in additional AI cloud contracts.

Meanwhile, Dell received an Outperform rating and $640 price target as RBC Capital Markets initiated coverage of the stock.

"DELL exited 2Q27 with $95bn in AI server backlog and a pipeline that continues to grow despite converting ~$132bn into orders over the LTM," said RBC analyst David Paige in an investor note. "We view the environment as supply-constrained (primarily memory) rather than demand-limited and expect a meaningful backlog to persist through FY27, providing visibility into FY28."

"Agentic AI is creating incremental CPU/traditional server demand to run orchestration layers, expanding the TAM for traditional compute," Paige added. "Additional vectors include enterprise server refresh (majority of installed base on 14G or older), PC refresh, data center consolidation, and AI inference migration. Large enterprises are entering multi-year arrangements (3-5 years) focused on securing supply access, suggesting visibility extends beyond near-term dynamics."

Meanwhile, RBC also initiated coverage on HP with a Sector Perform rating and a $33 target.

"We believe HPQ is well positioned to benefit from the confluence of AI PC adoption, the shift toward edge computing and enterprise requirements for data privacy, creating a multi-year tailwind for the PS segment," Paige noted. "HPQ is targeting AI PC shipments of 60-70% by FY27 (up from ~45% in 3Q26) as enterprises increasingly deploy local inference to address cloud token economics, latency constraints, and data governance requirements."

data.title: Joint Readout of Principals' Meeting of U.S. and UK Authorities Regarding Central Counterparty Resolution
data.description:
Washington, D.C.--(Newsfile Corp. - September 11, 2026) - Senior officials from the Securities and Exchange Commission, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, Commodity Futures Trading Commission, Federal Reserve Board, and Bank of England convened for a tabletop exercise on Sept. 3, 2026, to discuss certain issues relating to the hypothetical resolution of central counterparties (CCPs). This meeting was one of a regular series of senior-level meetings held since 2017 to share views on CCP resolution and review the progress of an ongoing program of joint work among the agencies.

The meeting was an opportunity to review recent joint work undertaken by the agencies, in particular the information sharing and communications arrangements to support financial stability in the event of a CCP resolution. Participants acknowledged the importance of continuing to facilitate a dialogue between UK and U.S. authorities and continuing to share analyses and discussing policy formulation in relation to CCP resolution.

data.title: Raw sugar slides off 16-month peak, arabica near 10-week low as ICE stocks set to rise
data.description:
Raw sugar futures slid off their 16-month peaks on Friday, looking to wipe out this weeks gains, while arabica coffee hovered near 10-week lows amid signs that exchange stocks are set to rise.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar fell 4% to 17.98 cents per lb at 1110 GMT, after hitting a 16-month peak of 18.88 cents on Thursday.

* The recent run up in sugar has been driven by tight supplies in India, Thailand, Europe and Brazil, as well as strength in energy markets, which can encourage more use of cane to make the biofuel ethanol rather than sugar.

* Oil prices fell on Friday but remained on track to close above $100 a barrel for the first time in nearly 4 months.

* Sugar production in Thailand, the world's second-largest exporter of the commodity after Brazil, is expected to fall 12.5% to 10.5 million metric tons in the 2026/27 season, an industry official said.

* White sugar fell 3.2% to $521 a ton.

COFFEE

* Arabica coffee slipped 0.2% to $2.8760 per lb, after setting a 10-week low of $2.8210 on Thursday.

* Traders are planning to deliver significant volumes of arabica coffee from the world's biggest producer Brazil to ICE exchange warehouses, where stocks have sunk to 26-year lows and driven up prices, dealers, brokers and analysts with knowledge of the matter said.

* Top grower Brazil exported a record volume of green coffee for August, shipping 3.82 million bags, a 31.7% jump compared with last year, industry group Cecafe said.

* This year's harvest in Brazil is now nearly complete and the focus was switching to prospects for the 2027 crop, which is off to a good start with ample rains favouring flowering.

* "The market may be short term oversold, but it has also broken below a two month trading range, and that projects to 240.85, another 40 cents lower from here," said broker ADMIS.

* Robusta coffee was little changed at $3,554 a ton.

COCOA

* London cocoa dipped 0.2% to £4,335 per ton.

* The market is consolidating after hitting a near one-year high earlier this month.

* ADMIS noted that top growers Ivory Coast and parts of Ghana have received some timely rainfall in recent days.

* New York cocoa fell 0.3% to $5,945 a ton.

data.title: Azerbaijan's Bank Respublika to acquire foreign-owned AccessBank in merger deal
data.description:
Azerbaijan's Bank Respublika has agreed to acquire AccessBank from a group of international financial institutions in a deal that will give AccessBank's current shareholders a combined 25% stake in Bank Respublika, the banks said on Friday.

AccessBank's shareholders include the Asian Development Bank, International Finance Corporation, European Investment Bank, Dutch development bank FMO, Austria's OeEB and funds managed by responsAbility.

Bank Respublika will acquire 100% of AccessBank's shares, with the transaction expected to close by November 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The two lenders will initially operate separately before merging, subject to regulatory requirements.

The combined bank will have assets of about 4.5 billion manats ($2.65 billion) and a loan portfolio of 3.3 billion manats.

data.title: Novo Nordisk Stock Falls as Morgan Stanley Doubts the Offset
data.description:
Novo Nordisk fell 1.23% premarket after Morgan Stanley downgraded it to Underweight from Equal-weight, keeping a 250 DKK target that implies more than 10% downside. Analysts led by Thibault Boutherin wrote that the valuation does not entirely reflect subdued mid-term growth or "the implications of the semaglutide patent cliff on Novo's terminal value." The shares fell 2% in Copenhagen trading.

Semaglutide, the ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, accounted for 75% of sales in 2026 and Morgan Stanley models it still at 59% in 2031, when loss of exclusivity starts to bite across Europe and the US. The bank sees the oral obesity franchise reaching $10 billion by 2031, which it says won't offset pricing and competitive headwinds. Its forecast is 2% to 3% revenue and EBIT growth in 2027 and a 4% compound annual rate through 2030, against 4% revenue and 7% EBIT growth for European pharma generally.

Novo trades at 12.5x 2027 estimated earnings, a 7% discount to European large pharma but a 35% premium to global peers with their own exclusivity problems, with Sanofi at 8x and GSK at 10x. A Morgan Stanley survey of 200 primary care physicians pointed to share losses to Eli Lilly Inc. over the next 18 months, including retatrutide expected in 2027.

Dividend alert, Sept. 11 -- Shares of Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Limited are likely to remain in focus in the coming week ahead of the upcoming dividend record date. Its shares ended lower on Friday and ended the week on a subdued note. The Gujarat-based PSU stock declined close to 2.42% over the past five trading sessions.

The Gujarat government-backed commodity chemicals firm had announced a 177% final dividend for financial year 2025-26. Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals dividend record date is scheduled for the coming week.

The company's board of directors had recommended a final dividend of Rs.17.7 per equity share with a face value of Rs.10 each for the financial year 2025-26. "The Record Date fixed for determining entitlement of Members to receive the dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 is Friday, 181h September, 2026," stated the firm in its BSE filing.

The company's Annual General Meeting (AGM) is set to be held on September 25. "The Dividend if approved by the Shareholders at the 53rd AGM shall be paid on or after Wednesday 30th September, 2026," as per the BSE filing.

The Gujarat PSU stock closed 1.53% lower at Rs.705.6 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.5,181.71 crore on Friday, September 11. The stock had touched an intraday high of Rs.716.50 per share and an intraday low of Rs.704.15 per share. The firm's return on equity (ROE) stood at 1.02%. data.title: Gas Prices Push Estimated Social Security Raise Higher — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Elizabeth O'Brien

Persistent inflation has pushed the projected Social Security raise for 2027 to 3.5%, the highest level in several years.

The estimate from Mary Johnson, an independent Social Security and Medicare policy analyst, comes as inflation held steady in August, rising 3.4% year over year on higher gas prices, according to the consumer price index data released Friday. The annual cost-of-living adjustment to Social Security is based on a CPI subset that increased 3.5% over the past 12 months.

The Social Security Administration typically announces the COLA for the coming year in October, when the third-quarter inflation data are complete. This year, that will fall on Oct. 14. The raise is calculated by comparing the average inflation rates for the third quarter of the current year and the previous year.

A boost of 3.5% would add $71 to the average monthly retirement benefit of $2,032. It would be the highest since the 8.7% COLA for 2023, which followed the inflation spike of the prior year.

Social Security is on shaky financial footing, and some proposals to close its funding shortfall involve modifying the COLA. One would impose a flat-rate COLA that would cut annual benefits by $285 in 2026 for the average beneficiary, according to an analysis from the AARP Public Policy Institute.

"Pay close attention to the debate over Social Security solvency now," Johnson said in a statement. "It's important for midterm voters to understand the changes to Social Security that members of Congress face to shore up the program."

If Congress fails to act, the retirement trust fund is projected to run dry in 2032, triggering an automatic benefit cut of 22%. That means that U.S. senators elected in this November's midterm election will likely be part of any fix that Congress passes before then.

Write to Elizabeth O'Brien at elizabeth.obrien@barrons.com

data.title: PE firm Waterland ends alliance with Giacom in Gamma takeover pursuit
data.description:
Dutch private equity firm Waterland said on Friday it is no longer in concert with UK-based Giacom to make an offer for British telecom company Gamma Communications .

Here are some more details:

  • Gamma agreed to a 1,120 pence per share offer from private equity firm Epiris earlier this month, capping months of takeover talks.

  • Waterland said it is continuing to consider its interest in Gamma, but that there can be no certainty of a firm offer.

  • Gamma's shares were down 2.8% at 1141p at 1443 GMT.

  • The telecommunications company has attracted interest from several private equity firms this year, including Oakley Capital and Providence Equity Partners, which withdrew their bids in June.

  • In August, Gamma said Giacom, a telecom service company, is acting in concert with Waterland relating to a possible deal in which Giacom would buy certain business units of Gamma.

  • The Sunday Times reported on Monday that Waterland could make an offer for Gamma that could exceed Epiris' £1.08 billion ($1.46 billion) bid.

  • Giacom could not be reached immediately for comment.

($1 = 0.7392 pounds)

data.title: Dollar edges higher against Swiss franc after US inflation data
data.description:
Key points:
  • U.S. consumer price index increased 0.4%
  • Fed rate odds reaches near 90%
  • Dollar on track for third straight weekly gain against Swiss franc

By Chibuike Oguh

The dollar edged higher against the Swiss franc on Friday after closely watched U.S. inflation data showed a rise in consumer prices, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week.

The dollar initially gained as the data boosted the likelihood of a rate hike. However, investor sentiment remained fragile as an escalating Middle East conflict pushed up oil prices, limiting the U.S. currency's advance and leaving it little changed against its peers.

Labor Department data showed that the U.S. consumer price index increased 0.4% in August after edging up 0.1% in July. The so-called core CPI increased 2.4% year-on-year in August after rising 2.5% in July.

The dollar rose broadly against the euro and Swiss franc before giving back some of those gains immediately after the data.

The euro was down 0.01% at $1.1611 and was on track for a weekly loss. The dollar strengthened 0.22% to 0.814 against the franc. It was set for its third straight weekly gain against the Swiss currency.

"The main thing we're looking at is core CPI, which seems to be accelerating," said Juan Perez, director of trading at MonexUSA.

"What that does do - which tends to help the U.S. dollar go up against all currencies - is increase the interest rate probability or odds that the Federal Reserve will raise rates at their next meeting."

Markets are now pricing in about an 86% chance of a 25 basis-point hike, compared with around 72% a day earlier, according to the CME's FedWatch tool.

U.S. Treasury yields remained near multi-year highs, with the 2-year yield, which typically moves in step with Fed rate expectations, up 5 basis points at 4.6%.

OIL REMAINS ABOVE $100

Brent crude oil prices were on track to rise more than 9% for the week after Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen's port city of Mocha and advanced down the Red Sea coast to strategic islands.

Brent crude futures were down 2.2% at $105.12 a barrel.

The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.04% to 99.04. It was set to drop 0.16% on the week — its second consecutive weekly drop.

YEN GAINS

The yen was on track for a second consecutive weekly gain against the U.S. dollar and was last up 0.51% at 153.58 per dollar.

The Bank of Japan is expected to raise interest rates next week and could signal a faster pace of future tightening if rising price pressures increase the risk of inflation overshooting its target, four sources familiar with its thinking told Reuters.

Japan's currency strengthened further after data released on Friday showed Japanese wholesale inflation remained elevated in August, reinforcing the case for a rate hike this month.

The euro weakened 0.57% against the yen to 178.28.
